item.title: Meet Asha Sharma: Indian-origin executive named CEO of Microsoft Gaming
item.description: Microsoft has appointed Asha Sharma as the new CEO of its gaming division, succeeding Phil Spencer. Sharma, with a background in AI and platform leadership, aims to refocus on Xbox's core audience amidst industry challenges like slowing revenue and intense competition. This significant leadership shift signals a strategic reset for Xbox.

item.title: ‘That could’ve been me’: Gordon Ramsay breaks down over brother’s heroin addiction in raw new Netflix series
item.description: With six episodes released, Being Gordon Ramsay offers an unfiltered portrait of the celebrity chef as he launches five restaurants in London’s 22 Bishopsgate. Beyond business, the series explores his turbulent childhood, violent alcoholic father and enduring guilt over his brother’s heroin addiction, revealing how proximity to failure continues to fuel his relentless drive.

item.title: Explained: 5 reasons why NYT op-ed is saying it's 'India's century'
item.description: India is emerging as a significant global player, challenging the US-China bipolar narrative. With a younger population and faster growth than China, India is positioning itself as a "third pole" in a "multiplex" world. Its strategy of "multi-alignment" allows it to engage with multiple powers while maintaining strategic autonomy, leveraging its growing diaspora as a diplomatic asset.

item.title: 'Deeply disappointing,' says Donald Trump on US Supreme Court striking down Tariffs - Top quotes
item.description: President Trump expressed deep disappointment and shame over the Supreme Court's ruling deeming his reciprocal tariffs illegal. He accused the court of being swayed by foreign interests and a small political movement, calling some justices "fools and lapdogs" for their perceived disloyalty to the constitution. This decision significantly impacts the President's trade war strategy.

item.title: Anonymous person donates $3.6 million in gold blocks to fix clogged drains and water system in Japan's Osaka
item.description: An anonymous benefactor gifted Osaka 21 kilograms of gold, valued at $3.6 million, specifically for water and drainage system repairs. This significant donation, accepted after thorough checks, will address urgent infrastructure needs in the aging Japanese city's network, which serves millions and faces frequent failures. Officials expressed immense gratitude for the timely and substantial support.

item.title: Epstein Files: From beheadings to murder - why former prince Andrew arrest is mild by Europe's bloody history of royal treatment
item.description: Former prince Andrew’s legal troubles linked to the Epstein Files may seem dramatic in today’s news cycle, but European history tells a far darker story of how disgraced royals were once treated. From English kings who were imprisoned and executed, to French monarchs guillotined before cheering crowds, and Russian tsars wiped out along with their families, royal downfall traditionally meant violent ends rather than court cases. The contrast highlights how monarchy has transformed over centuries — from an institution sustained by power and fear to one constrained by law, public opinion, and media scrutiny, where scandal now leads to reputational damage instead of bloodshed.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Extremely brave’: Trump jokes about giving himself the Congressional Medal of Honor — is it possible?
item.description: Former President Donald Trump humorously suggested he considered awarding himself the Congressional Medal of Honor after a 2018 visit to US troops in Iraq. He acknowledged this would be a significant stretch, as the award is reserved for military personnel demonstrating extreme bravery. Trump mentioned he might "test the law" someday.

item.title: Indian-American Jay Bhattacharya to head CDC in addition to NIH
item.description: President Trump has appointed Indian-American Dr. Jay Bhattacharya to lead both the NIH and CDC, a first for federal health leadership. This consolidation aims to synchronize health policy, bridging research and implementation. Bhattacharya, a physician and health economist, previously co-authored the Great Barrington Declaration, advocating against universal Covid -19 lockdowns.

item.title: 'False prophet of our time': Iran's exiled prince Reza Pahlavi slams Khamenei's 'illegitimate' regime; urges Shias to 'reclaim faith'
item.description: Exiled Prince Reza Pahlavi has strongly criticized Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, accusing the Islamic Republic of betraying its people and faith. He urged Shia Muslims to reclaim their religion from what he called the "false prophet of our time," highlighting the regime's repression and violence. Pahlavi also called for unity among all Iranians, including minorities, against the current leadership.
